item.description:
Kento Beta 1.0, build 3292

Kento's first beta: from this version on, "Beta" stands where "Alpha" did.

New

  • Kiri's see-through subject, for smoke, glass and anything else the screen shows through (Edge, under 4K in tiles): the edge becomes how far the plate differs from the screen behind it, in place of the model's matte, which leaves smoke nearly empty and calls glass solid. On the studio's test shots, where the screen shows through, the error went from 0.261 to 0.109 on smoke and from 0.817 to 0.098 on glass. Connect a clean plate first, and leave it off for hair and fur.

Changed

  • The Viewer's guides can be seen: they draw at full strength in their colors (they had been faint whatever the color), any color through Custom..., and a lines row sets their strength, width (1 to 3 px) and mode: Normal, Outlined (a dark edge either side, readable on any picture) or Difference.
  • Zoomed out, a node's ports stay where their wires meet it: the ring you aim at is the one the wire arrives at, nothing jumps. Each input takes the stretch of the node's edge nearest it, so a press needn't hit the ring; the one it would take is lit and named. On a busy node (Kiri, a Merge with several A inputs), a wire dropped anywhere on it opens a short list of its inputs by name; Settings > Node Graph > Busy Nodes: Choose Input From A List turns it off.
  • Errors show in Kento's own sheet, dropped from the top of the window: what didn't happen in plain words, what happened and what to do, each error and warning as a row (a node's name selects it), the technical details folded with Copy details, and Report a problem.
  • Copy and paste are Kento's own: Cmd+C and Cmd+V copy and paste nodes with everything kept, and text on the clipboard that isn't nodes copied in Kento is never run. For Nuke, Edit > Copy for Nuke (Shift+Cmd+C) and Paste from Nuke (Shift+Cmd+V).
  • Kiri's MEMatte refinement is now a choice a shot, refine hair, off until you turn it on. 0.9.48 and 0.9.49 ran it on every shot of the General route; measured against the true mattes of eight test shots, it helped a hair shot and a portrait (their error over the frame 0.0129 to 0.0101 and 0.040 to 0.030) but made fur, a walking figure and leaves a little worse. Turn it on for hair and compare. It works in 4K tiles too.

Fixed

  • An update no longer waits forever when the old Kento gets stuck quitting: the new one goes in once the old one has stopped running. (This takes effect from this version's updater on.)
  • Working out a shot of two or three frames on Kiri's General route failed with "missing profile files": such ranges are now padded to the four frames CorridorKey works on at a time.

Kento Alpha 0.9.49, build 3240

Changed

  • Kiri's MEMatte refinement now works on every Mac: its weights (111 MB) come down from Kento's own download site the first time you work out a shot with the General route, checked against the authors' file. It needs Kento's seat; if the download fails, CorridorKey's matte is used and the line under the button says why.
  • Nagi's learned method: its tooltip and the manual now say it's made for path-traced CG renders. On the studio's real camera plates non-local means took out more noise (3.5 dB against learned's 1.8 on one plate; on another learned made it slightly worse), so keep non-local means for camera plates and grain.
  • The Lens node reads ARRI's own lens metadata from a plate (its focal lengths and focus distance under ARRI's names), so a plate from an ALEXA names its lens where it didn't before.

Kento Alpha 0.9.48, build 3227

New

  • Kiri's depth defocus works: it softens the foreground to the plate's focus. Match to background (or setting depth defocus the first time) measures how much softer the background's edges are than the foreground's own, and depth defocus puts that share of the blur on the foreground over the plate; the line under it says what it measured. On a test plate blurred by 3 px it measured 2.8.
  • Kiri's General route refines CorridorKey's edge with MEMatte where CorridorKey is unsure, the studio's best recipe for hair (on its tests, the edge's error 0.165 to 0.139, for about a third of a second a frame). It runs when MEMatte's weights are in Kento's models folder; Install doesn't offer them yet.

Changed

  • VectorRetime's Motion is sharper and quicker: its flow is now worked out to about 1,000 pixels across rather than at full size, which on footage with true in-between frames scored better (2K 34.0 to 34.5 dB, 4K 32.4 to 33.4).
  • LightKey's Screen Grow/Shrink grows the matte as NukeX does: level by level, each level's pixels joined. On RAI_150 the windshield key went from 0.052 off NukeX's to 0.0018, the front edge from 0.031 to 0.0047. Half-pixel sizes still differ a little at some corners.
  • Reconcile3D's clamp works as NukeX's: negatives to 0, values over 1 kept.
  • Nuke scripts' menus answer as in Nuke: a menu's items come in its own order and getValue() gives the item's index (VectorRetime's Output Speed had read 2, not 0), and menus made from Gaffer's preset lists are found. Kento's own Python API (kento) now sits under the nuke module, and render nodes have it too.
  • Nagi's learned method: the tooltip and manual now say to keep non-local means for grainy plates. On fine film grain it takes out about twice as much as learned; learned is the cleanest on even sensor noise.

Fixed

  • Gaffer's hash cache is capped at about a tenth of the machine's memory: on a deep comp it could hold some 4 million entries on every thread, about 20 GB on a 16-core Mac (MC1_050's frozen Kento); now about 7 GB at most there. Comps render as fast as before; MC1_050's slowest nodes are still slow where Gaffer works them out.
